source: Seams follow CodeHS Video Game Design in JavaScript 3.2 Program Structure, 3.3 The Canvas, 3.4 Your First Sprites. Structure only: no CodeHS text, problems or code is copied.

lessons.title: The frame loop
lessons.objective: Students will be able to say what runs once and what runs every frame, and read a sketch that has both setup() and draw().

lessons.title: The canvas and the sprite
lessons.objective: Students will be able to create a canvas, put a sprite on it, keep that sprite in a variable, and name the properties that position and paint it.

lessons.title: Hello Sprite
lessons.objective: Students will be able to build a sketch of their own that draws one sprite, and explain which line of it runs once and which runs every frame.

lessons.title: Keyboard input and velocity
lessons.objective: Students will be able to read a key with kb.pressing() using either WASD or arrow-key names, turn that reading into a velocity, and predict where the sprite goes next frame.

lessons.title: The else-to-zero rule
lessons.objective: Students will be able to explain why a sprite keeps drifting when the else branch is missing, and build four-direction keyboard movement that stops when no key is held.

lessons.title: Build it and prove it
lessons.objective: Students will be able to put words on the canvas with text(), make a sprite move on its own with frameCount and sin(), build the sprite playground and its second auto-moving sprite, write the frame-loop explanation, and take on the stretch challenges.

lessons.title: Optional: a grid like math
lessons.objective: Students will be able to read a coordinate grid over the canvas, and say where (0, 0) is and which way y grows in the default mode and in the optional math mode.
